services.seoTitle: How car painting and bodywork work at Mpaint

seoSteps.p: Before painting, we assess the extent of the damage, the condition of the body panel and the existing paint. If needed, we remove rust, repair dents, and prepare the surface with sanding, priming and other preparatory work.
The paint is chosen to match the car's factory colour code and existing shade. We paint individual body parts such as bumpers, doors, wings and bonnets, as well as larger body surfaces and full cars.
Alongside car painting, we carry out body repair, welding, rust damage repair, dent removal, part replacement and polishing. The scope of work depends on the car's condition and the type of damage.

faq.q: Can a scratch be repaired without repainting the whole panel?
faq.a: Sometimes, yes. It depends on how deep the scratch is and the condition of the paint layer.

faq.q: Can a dent be removed without repainting?
faq.a: Yes, if the paint layer is intact and the damage allows for paintless dent removal.

faq.q: How is rust damage repaired?
faq.a: We remove the affected area, repair the metal if needed, and prepare the surface for repainting.

faq.q: Can a rusted part always be repaired?
faq.a: Not always. A severely damaged or fully rusted-through part may need partial or full replacement.

faq.q: How is the new paint matched to the existing colour?
faq.a: We start from your car's factory colour code and check the tone against the existing paintwork.

faq.q: Can plastic bumpers be repaired and painted?
faq.a: Yes. Whether it's possible depends on the extent of any cracks, deformation, or other damage.

faq.q: Do you also paint whole cars?
faq.a: Yes, we paint individual parts as well as larger areas and full cars.

faq.q: What's done before painting?
faq.a: The surface is cleaned, sanded, repaired and primed according to its condition.

faq.q: What bodywork services do you offer?
faq.a: We repair dents, rust and body damage, carry out welding, and prepare surfaces for painting.

faq.q: How long does the work take?
faq.a: It depends on the extent of the damage, the preparation needed, and the scope of the repair.

accident.h1: Car damaged in an accident? Bodywork and painting in Tallinn
accident.intro: After an accident, it is often hard to judge how extensive the damage really is. Here is what Mpaint takes into account for post-accident bodywork and painting, and how to get a damaged car to our workshop.

sections.heading: What kind of damage needs inspecting
paragraphs: Visible damage, such as dents, scratches, a cracked bumper, or a loose body part, is the easiest to notice. But even a minor collision can affect the car's alignment or structure in a way that does not show from the outside. If the car was involved in an accident, it is worth having it inspected even if the damage looks minor.

sections.heading: How to request a quote
paragraphs: The easiest way to start is by sending us photos of the damage. The more angles and the better the lighting, the more accurate our initial estimate can be.

sections.heading: Why photos help with the initial assessment
paragraphs: Photos give us an initial picture of the type and extent of the damage and help decide whether it is purely cosmetic or needs a more thorough inspection. This speeds up the process and lets us give a preliminary estimate before the car even arrives at the workshop.

sections.heading: When an in-person inspection is needed
paragraphs: For a more serious accident, suspected structural damage, or several damaged areas, photos alone are not enough. In that case we only give an exact quote after seeing the car, since the real extent of the damage often only becomes clear during an in-person inspection.

sections.heading: Why some damage does not show from the outside
paragraphs: The force of a collision does not always stay contained to the visible impact point. It can affect the car's structure or alignment even if only a small dent or scratch is visible from the outside.

sections.heading: How bodywork, parts replacement, and painting fit together
paragraphs: Post-accident repair often involves several stages together: repairing or replacing damaged body parts, rust protection where needed, and always painting, so the colour matches the rest of the car.

accident.safetyNote: If the steering feels harder to turn after an accident, the car pulls to one side while driving, you hear an unusual sound when braking, or a body or plastic part is loose, the car should not be driven any further.
accident.towingHeading: Car not drivable after an accident?
accident.towingText: If your car cannot be driven safely after an accident, it can be transported directly to the Mpaint workshop by a recovery provider. Please contact us before arranging delivery so we can coordinate receiving the vehicle.

faq.q: Does Mpaint handle insurance claims?
faq.a: No, we do not handle insurance claims or on-site accident assistance. Our job is the bodywork and paint repair itself.

faq.q: Do you offer a towing service?
faq.a: No, Mpaint does not provide towing itself. We recommend using a suitable recovery or towing service, and we will give you the workshop address and agree on a delivery time.

faq.q: Is post-accident bodywork different from regular repair?
faq.a: We use the same welding and sheet-metal techniques as for regular bodywork. The difference is in the assessment: after an accident, it matters more to pin down whether the damage is purely cosmetic or affects the car's structure.

faq.q: How long does post-accident repair take?
faq.a: A typical post-accident repair takes roughly 3-4 working days, depending on the extent of the damage. This is an indicative timeframe, not a guarantee. Longer jobs, hidden damage, and parts delivery times can affect the schedule. We give an exact timeframe after we see the damage.

faq.a: Painting a single part, such as a bumper, takes 3-4 days on average.

faq.q: Does a cracked bumper need repairing before painting?
faq.a: Yes. Cracks and deformation are repaired before sanding and painting, otherwise the damage will show through the paint again.

faq.q: Can plastic bumpers even be painted?
